title: Psalms Chapter 31 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 31 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 31 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 31.

questions.question: In Psalms 31, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Put my trust in the LORD
Bow down thine ear to me
Pull me out of the net
questions.correctAnswer: Put my trust in the LORD
questions.explanation: The first mention in Psalms 31 is the act of putting trust in the LORD as stated in verse 1.

questions.question: Who is the psalm attributed to?
questions.explanation: The psalm is specifically described as 'A Psalm of David' in verse 1.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do regarding his trust?
options: Set my feet in a large room
questions.explanation: The psalmist requests deliverance in the context of trusting the LORD in verse 1.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do with his ear?
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks for the LORD to bow down His ear in verse 2.

questions.question: What is the psalmist's strong rock referred to in the text?
questions.explanation: The psalmist refers to the LORD as his strong rock in verse 2.

questions.question: For whose name's sake does the psalmist ask to be led and guided?
questions.explanation: The psalmist mentions asking to be led and guided for the LORD's name's sake in verse 3.

questions.question: What does the psalmist want the LORD to pull him out of?
questions.explanation: The psalmist specifically asks to be pulled out of the net in verse 4.

questions.question: Into whose hands does the psalmist commit his spirit?
questions.explanation: The psalmist commits his spirit into the LORD's hands in verse 5.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say he has hated?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states he has hated them that regard lying vanities in verse 6.

questions.question: What has the LORD considered according to the psalmist?
questions.explanation: The psalmist mentions that the LORD has considered his troubles in verse 7.

questions.question: What has the LORD not done to the psalmist according to verse 8?
options: Shut him up into the hand of the enemy
questions.correctAnswer: Shut him up into the hand of the enemy
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that the LORD has not shut him up into the hand of the enemy in verse 8.

questions.question: The psalmist rejoices in the LORD's what?
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses gladness and rejoices in the LORD's mercy in verse 7.

questions.question: The psalmist has been shut up into the hand of the enemy according to the text.
questions.explanation: The text states that the LORD has not shut the psalmist up into the hand of the enemy in verse 8.

questions.question: The psalmist trusts in lying vanities according to the text.
questions.explanation: The psalmist states he has hated those who regard lying vanities in verse 6, indicating he does not trust them.

questions.question: The psalmist has committed his strength into the hands of the enemy.
questions.explanation: The psalmist has committed his spirit into the hands of the LORD, not the enemy, as stated in verse 5.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 31 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 31 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the Lord to have upon him in Psalms 31:9?
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks for mercy because he is in trouble, as stated in Psalms 31:9.

questions.question: What does Psalms 31:10 indicate will happen if one acknowledges their iniquity?
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:10 says that the psalmist's strength faileth because of his iniquity.

questions.question: In Psalms 31:11, how does the psalmist describe his reputation among others?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that he was a reproach among all his enemies and neighbors, according to Psalms 31:11.

questions.question: What does Psalms 31:12 suggest about the psalmist's emotional state?
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses feeling forgotten as a dead man, illustrating his despair in Psalms 31:12.

questions.question: According to Psalms 31:13, what was the psalmist facing from those around him?
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:13 reveals that the psalmist heard the slander of many and was surrounded by fear.

questions.question: What does the psalmist declare in Psalms 31:14 about his trust?
questions.explanation: The psalmist explicitly states his trust in the Lord in Psalms 31:14.

questions.question: What does Psalms 31:15 emphasize about the psalmist's situation?
options: His times are in God's hands
questions.correctAnswer: His times are in God's hands
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:15 emphasizes that the psalmist's times are in God's hands, highlighting his reliance on God.

questions.question: In Psalms 31:16, what does the psalmist ask God to do for him?
options: Make his face shine upon him
questions.correctAnswer: Make his face shine upon him
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks God to make His face shine upon him in Psalms 31:16, seeking divine favor.

questions.question: What is the connection between Psalms 31:1 and Psalms 31:2 regarding trust?
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:1 shows trust in the Lord, and Psalms 31:2 asks for deliverance, indicating that trust leads to deliverance.

questions.question: What does Psalms 31:7 suggest about God's response to the psalmist's troubles?
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:7 indicates that God has considered the psalmist's troubles, showing His attentiveness.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'I am like a broken vessel' in Psalms 31:12 imply about the psalmist's condition?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'broken vessel' implies fragility and a feeling of being damaged, as stated in Psalms 31:12.

questions.question: What does Psalms 31:6 reveal about the psalmist's feelings towards those who engage in deceit?
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:6 shows that the psalmist has hated those who regard lying vanities, indicating his disdain for deceit.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist feels that God has abandoned him.
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses trust in God despite his troubles, indicating he does not feel abandoned, particularly in Psalms 31:14.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist believes that his enemies will eventually bring him peace.
questions.explanation: The psalmist is asking for deliverance from his enemies, indicating he does not believe they will bring him peace, as seen in Psalms 31:15.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist acknowledges his own iniquity in Psalms 31:10.
questions.explanation: The psalmist acknowledges his iniquity as a reason for his failing strength in Psalms 31:10.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 31 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 31.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD not to let happen to him in Psalms 31:17?
questions.explanation: The psalmist specifically pleads with the LORD, 'Let me not be ashamed,' indicating his trust and reliance on God for deliverance (Psalms 31:17).

questions.question: In Psalms 31:18, what does the psalmist want to happen to lying lips?
options: They should be put to silence
questions.correctAnswer: They should be put to silence
questions.explanation: The psalmist desires that the 'lying lips' be silenced as they speak against the righteous (Psalms 31:18).

questions.question: According to Psalms 31:19, what has God laid up for those who fear Him?
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes the great goodness God has prepared for those who fear Him (Psalms 31:19).

questions.question: In Psalms 31:20, what does God promise to do for the faithful?
questions.explanation: The psalmist notes that God will hide the faithful in His presence, indicating protection from the strife of tongues (Psalms 31:20).

questions.question: What is the response of the psalmist in Psalms 31:21 towards the LORD?
questions.explanation: The psalmist acknowledges the LORD's kindness and praises Him by saying, 'Blessed be the LORD' (Psalms 31:21).

questions.question: In Psalms 31:22, what did the psalmist express in his haste?
options: I am cut off from before thine eyes
questions.correctAnswer: I am cut off from before thine eyes
questions.explanation: In a moment of distress, the psalmist reveals his feeling of being cut off from God, yet recognizes God's attentiveness (Psalms 31:22).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'tov' (טוֹב) in Psalms 31:19 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Tov' means 'good' in Hebrew, reflecting God's benevolence toward those who fear Him (Psalms 31:19).

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Psalms 31:17-18?
questions.explanation: The verses use parallelism, contrasting the psalmist's plea with the fate of the wicked (Psalms 31:17-18).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of God's goodness in Psalms 31:19?
questions.explanation: James 1:17 states that every good gift comes from God, echoing the theme of divine goodness found in Psalms 31:19.

questions.question: Which other passage reflects the idea of God hiding His faithful in Psalms 31:20?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:20 speaks of hiding away for safety, similar to the protection promised in Psalms 31:20.

questions.question: What comes immediately before the declaration in Psalms 31:23?
options: For I said in my haste
questions.correctAnswer: For I said in my haste
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:22 precedes the call to love the LORD, indicating the psalmist's emotional state before expressing praise (Psalms 31:23).

questions.question: What does Psalms 31:24 encourage the faithful to do?
questions.explanation: The psalmist encourages the faithful to be courageous, trusting that the LORD will strengthen their hearts (Psalms 31:24).

questions.question: The LORD is said to preserve whom in Psalms 31:23?
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:23 states that the LORD preserves the faithful, contrasting with the fate of the proud doers.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist expresses doubt about God's ability to save in Psalms 31:22.
questions.explanation: The psalmist, despite expressing distress, acknowledges God's ability to hear his supplications, showing trust rather than doubt (Psalms 31:22).

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist wishes for the wicked to be ashamed in Psalms 31:17.
questions.explanation: The psalmist explicitly desires for the wicked to be ashamed and silenced, indicating a longing for justice (Psalms 31:17).

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 31 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 31 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 31:1 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is grounded in God's righteousness
Salvation is earned by human merit
Salvation is solely through human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is grounded in God's righteousness
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:1 states 'deliver me in thy righteousness,' indicating that salvation is based on God's righteous character, not human works.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin does Psalms 31:10 teach?
options: Sin causes spiritual and physical weakening
Sin is only a minor failing with no consequences
Sin leads primarily to social ostracism but no spiritual harm
questions.correctAnswer: Sin causes spiritual and physical weakening
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:10 says 'my strength faileth because of mine iniquity,' connecting sin with loss of strength and affliction.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's providence does Psalms 31:15 teach?
options: God sovereignly controls the believer's times and deliverance
God is indifferent to human suffering
Human destiny is random and uncontrolled
God's providence is limited to natural events only
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly controls the believer's times and deliverance
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:15 states 'My times are in thy hand,' affirming God's sovereign governance over life events.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 31:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:5 says 'Into thine hand I commit my spirit,' showing confidence in God's trustworthy nature to care for the soul.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 31:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:7 rejoices 'in thy mercy,' highlighting God's compassionate and merciful character.

questions.question: How does Psalms 31:4 connect to the broader biblical theme of God's protection?
options: It prefigures Christ as the protector who rescues from spiritual traps
It teaches that protection comes only through human effort
It denies God's involvement in human affairs
It emphasizes self-reliance over divine help
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Christ as the protector who rescues from spiritual traps
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:4 asks God to 'Pull me out of the net,' symbolizing God's deliverance from spiritual danger, a theme fulfilled in Christ's salvific work.

questions.question: How does Psalms 31:20 prepare for the New Testament understanding of God's presence?
options: It anticipates believers being hidden in God's presence from worldly strife
It limits God's presence to the temple only
It portrays God's presence as inaccessible
It teaches that God's presence is irrelevant for believers
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates believers being hidden in God's presence from worldly strife
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:20 speaks of hiding 'in the secret of thy presence,' prefiguring New Testament teaching on being secure in Christ’s presence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Psalms 31:1 and Psalms 31:14 teach about trust in God?
options: Trusting God is both a declaration of faith and a reliance on His righteousness
Trust in God is irrelevant to salvation
Trust in God is a human invention to cope with fear
Trust in God guarantees physical health and wealth
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God is both a declaration of faith and a reliance on His righteousness
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:1 emphasizes trust in God's righteousness; Psalms 31:14 expresses verbal affirmation of God as Lord, combining faith and dependence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 31:7 and Psalms 31:21 teach about God's kindness?
options: God's kindness is both a cause for rejoicing and an active protection in times of trouble
God's kindness is conditional on human merit
God's kindness is only symbolic and not practical
God's kindness is reserved for the proud and powerful
questions.correctAnswer: God's kindness is both a cause for rejoicing and an active protection in times of trouble
questions.explanation: Verse 7 rejoices in mercy; verse 21 praises God for kindness shown in a strong city, indicating active divine protection.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 31:18 and Psalms 31:23 teach about God's justice and judgment?
options: God silences the proud lying lips and rewards the faithful while punishing the proud doer
God ignores the wicked and rewards only the rich
God punishes sin without regard to repentance
questions.correctAnswer: God silences the proud lying lips and rewards the faithful while punishing the proud doer
questions.explanation: Verse 18 calls for silencing lying lips; verse 23 states the Lord rewards the proud doer, affirming divine justice.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Psalms 31:9-13 only expresses despair without hope. What does Psalms 31:9-13 actually teach?
options: They express honest suffering but also trust and hope in God's deliverance
They teach that despair is final and God does not intervene
They encourage abandoning faith due to suffering
They deny the reality of enemies and trials
questions.correctAnswer: They express honest suffering but also trust and hope in God's deliverance
questions.explanation: Though verses 9-13 detail trouble and enemies, the psalmist continues to trust God (see 31:14) showing hope amid suffering.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 31:19 teach about God's covenantal goodness?
options: God stores up great goodness for those who fear and trust Him
God's goodness is arbitrary and not related to fear or trust
God's goodness is only for Israel physically
God's goodness depends on human performance
questions.correctAnswer: God stores up great goodness for those who fear and trust Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:19 speaks of God's great goodness laid up for those who fear and trust Him, indicating covenantal blessing.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 31:3 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:3 calls God 'my rock and my fortress' and asks Him to lead and guide, showing God's faithfulness to His people.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is taught in Psalms 31:6?
options: The believer hates falsehood and trusts in the Lord, indicating a sanctified mind
Sanctification happens without any moral response
Sanctification is irrelevant to trust in God
questions.correctAnswer: The believer hates falsehood and trusts in the Lord, indicating a sanctified mind
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:6 says 'I have hated them that regard lying vanities; but I trust in the LORD,' showing moral rejection of falsehood as part of sanctification.

questions.question: How does Psalms 31:24 encourage believers in their spiritual journey?
options: By calling them to courage and promising strength for those who hope in the LORD
By urging them to rely solely on themselves
By teaching that hope in the LORD is futile
By encouraging avoidance of all trials
questions.correctAnswer: By calling them to courage and promising strength for those who hope in the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 31:24 commands courage and promises strengthened hearts for those who place hope in God, encouraging perseverance.
